title: Ballrooms and Battles of Music with Shaw
summary: Territory bands played for the Schribmans' ballrooms and colleges; Leeman describes Battles of Music, Shaw against Bunny Berigan and Red Norvo.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Wow! I can remember some of the black bands that Chick Webb and Cab Calloway and Coleman Hawkins were in -- man, if you go up to New England, look out for that Mel Hallis' band, becuase they had some bad cats in there. They flew every big name band down there, it was always a band contest when you ran into Mel Hallis' band. Now excuse me, Cliff, it's your life, you tell it.

No, I'm just a little bit later on -- because they were all around, the territory bands, they called them territory bands because they played for the Shripmans, and it's their territory, but there were lots of colleges to play in then and ballrooms -- oh, just ballrooms galore, all over -- those were the days of contact dancing.
And of course, Glenn Miller came along as a territory band.
Did you ever play with Glenn Miller?

No, I was supposed to go with him -- I was just getting to that before. And then there was Bunny Berigan. Shripman used to put us on, used to have every once a week, or every two or three weeks, he'd put us in a ballroom like down in Connecticut.
Now wait, you say 'us' -- who was 'us', Cliff?

And they had what they called Battles of Music. So we would battle, maybe Bunny Berigan was forming a band then, playing the territories. And Battles of Music was something that would draw a lot of musicians and people; they'd come to see what one band would do against another. We had Battles of Music with Shaw against Red Norvo and his whole band, and so forth and so on.
